listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Friday, October 23. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is about Iran. The United States and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November, after the U.S. midterm elections. A person briefed on war planning told NPR this. Iran has said it is prepared. The report describes planning for a possible attack, not a final decision. Now the front page. Anthropic is donating the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation, under the Linux Foundation. The company says it will stay open, community driven and vendor neutral. In architecture, Revizto's MCP server comes packaged with reusable Claude skills. They are modelled on how project teams actually work. In politics, a federal judge restricted Department of Homeland Security field operations that look for noncitizen voters. The judge found they likely violated the Voting Rights Act, which bars voter intimidation. And the San Francisco 49ers visit Atlanta on Sunday. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris returns to the city. His undefeated team will try to pressure Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Junior. Now the sections. In tech, Claude Models on Google Cloud has launched, and Anthropic's knowledge work plugins bring role-based skills to Claude Cowork. In politics, Drop Site News reports on leaked documents about a UAE project to list Facebook users. NPR reports that the administration is considering moving the White House press corps out of the White House. In world news, a study says record heat in Europe this summer helped kill more than 50,000 people. Typhoon Champi shut down Taiwan, with hundreds of flights cancelled. And officials say the Ebola patients in Nigeria and Kenya both passed through Entebbe airport on October third. In sports, the Rockets held Kyrie Irving to 15 points in a 128 to 110 win over Dallas. UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi features two title fights. And this year's World Series will crown a first-time winner. In Atlanta, Urbanize Atlanta looks at the city's newest baseball venue as it takes shape. Investment continues near the city's historically Black colleges. And a new lawsuit makes corruption allegations against College Park and two council members. In architecture, AEC Magazine looks at AI tools for building code compliance. Qonic is edging toward full BIM authoring. And Arcadis is automating engineering reviews with Nomic. In science, satellite records now let researchers compare this year's El Niño with the strongest ones before it. Hubble is preparing the way for the Roman Space Telescope. And googly-eyed buoys are helping keep seabirds out of fishing nets. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: U.S. and Israel are planning for a possible attack on Iran, source tells NPR
lead.note: The United States and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November, after the U.S. midterm elections. That is according to a person briefed on war planning, who spoke to NPR. Iran has said it is prepared. The report describes planning for a possible attack, not a decision to carry one out. The timing, after the midterms, is the central detail in the account. For a reader who wants a short, neutral read on major world news, this is the item most likely to shape the wider picture in the coming weeks, because it involves two governments and a possible military action. It is worth watching for any official confirmation, denial or response from the governments named, since the report rests on a single source briefed on the planning.
lead.headline: US, Israel Plan Possible Iran Attack
decks: Plans point to early November, after U.S. midterm elections.
